drafts.headline: Depreciation forecast from an asset base that is itself forecast compounds its own error.
drafts.plain: Depreciation is usually projected as a rate on a fixed-asset balance that the model has also projected. Two forecasts stacked on each other drift much further than either one alone.
drafts.evidence: Bias +0.586 log (about 1.8 times too high), average miss 1.112, wrong in the same direction in 77% of cases, and the sign holds across every bootstrap block tested (n=39).
drafts.why_scope: A robust bias in one driver may be this company's disclosure, its whole class's economics, or our method. Decide which before filing.
drafts.overturned_by: A build where depreciation is taken from a disclosed schedule rather than from a projected asset base, and the error stays large.

drafts.headline: Finance cost forecasts run about 2.9 times too low for PHDC.
drafts.plain: The method misses this driver in the same direction almost every time, not at random. That is a fixable defect rather than noise — find what is wired wrong before adding any correction factor.
drafts.evidence: Bias -1.074 log (about 2.9 times too low), average miss 1.076, wrong in the same direction in 97% of cases, and the sign holds across every bootstrap block tested (n=32).
drafts.why_scope: A robust bias in one driver may be this company's disclosure, its whole class's economics, or our method. Decide which before filing.
drafts.overturned_by: A later run of the same name where the sign no longer holds across bootstrap blocks.
drafts.declined: already registered as L-204 (PHDC's interest must be measured on the borrowings that actually bear interest) and as L-002 (a correction factor is only honest when the model is right)

drafts.headline: A developer's new-sales value is under-forecast whenever price and volume are projected separately.
drafts.plain: Sales value is units times price. Project each one conservatively and the two shortfalls multiply, so the value comes out much lower than it should. Check the product, not just the parts.
drafts.evidence: Bias -0.369 log (about 45% too low), average miss 0.480, wrong in the same direction in 66% of cases, and the sign holds across every bootstrap block tested (n=35).
drafts.why_scope: A robust bias in one driver may be this company's disclosure, its whole class's economics, or our method. Decide which before filing.
drafts.overturned_by: A developer where price and volume are projected jointly and the value forecast is still biased low.

drafts.headline: The net profit forecast loses to assuming no change.
drafts.plain: At 5 of 5 horizons, simply carrying last year's number forward beat the model. A method that cannot beat 'no change' has not earned the precision it displays, and should be published as a range or not at all.
drafts.evidence: Negative skill against the freeze benchmark at horizons 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, worst -3.827.
drafts.why_scope: Losing to a naive benchmark usually points at the method, which would make it ALL — but confirm it is not this company's series being unusually persistent.
drafts.overturned_by: A later run where the model beats the freeze benchmark at a majority of horizons.
drafts.declined: already registered as L-001 and L-011 — the naive-benchmark loss is the evidence behind both, not a separate lesson

drafts.headline: The depreciation and amortisation error is the company, not the currency.
drafts.plain: Re-running every forecast with perfect foresight of inflation barely improves it. So devaluation is not the explanation, and looking for a macro fix would waste the effort.
drafts.evidence: Average miss 1.112 as known, 1.107 with perfect foresight of inflation — the macro share is only 0.4%.
drafts.why_scope: Almost always ALL — 'check whether the macro explains it before assuming it does' is a method rule — but the specific finding may be about this market.
drafts.overturned_by: A market or period where the same decomposition puts most of the error on the macro path.
drafts.declined: same finding as the line above; the macro decomposition is recorded once

drafts.headline: A bias that changes direction between regimes must never be corrected for.
drafts.plain: If a driver runs high in one period and low in the next, the average is a number that was never true. Record the instability and leave the driver alone.
drafts.evidence: By era: E1 pre-float -0.315; E2 post-float +0.089; E3 devaluation -0.015.
drafts.why_scope: A sign that flips with the regime is usually about the market or the period, not the company — but say which.
drafts.overturned_by: A record long enough that one sign dominates across every regime tested.

drafts.headline: Test every measured bias for stability across regimes before acting on it.
drafts.plain: A bias measured over a whole history can hide two opposite halves. Split the record by regime and check the sign holds in both before you treat it as a fact.
drafts.evidence: By era: E2 post-float +0.507; E3 devaluation -0.196.
drafts.why_scope: A sign that flips with the regime is usually about the market or the period, not the company — but say which.
drafts.overturned_by: Nothing. This is a rule about how to read a measured bias.

drafts.headline: The units sold bias changes direction between regimes.
drafts.plain: It runs one way in one period and the other way in the next. Averaging them produces a correction that is wrong in both. Record it, do not correct for it.
drafts.evidence: By era: E1 pre-float +0.173; E2 post-float -0.091; E3 devaluation -0.490.
drafts.why_scope: A sign that flips with the regime is usually about the market or the period, not the company — but say which.
drafts.overturned_by: A longer record in which one sign dominates across all regimes.
drafts.declined: the units-sold era flip is the launch-calendar effect already registered as L-101
